query: Across role, grade level, and subject, which open-response themes are associated with satisfaction?

per_column.name: teacher_adaptation_to_remote_format
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated ordinal-ish categories (creative_innovation → not_evident) extracted from open responses; a plausible external theme that can be segmented and compared against satisfaction.

per_column.name: instructional_depth_vs_compliance
per_column.rationale: Clear graded categories (conceptual_mastery → not_apparent) with balanced counts; an associational theme distinct from the satisfaction score, supporting grouped comparison.

per_column.name: participation_barriers
per_column.rationale: Distinct barrier types (cognitive_overload, technical_interference, etc.) with reasonable spread; interpretable segmentation to relate to satisfaction.

per_column.name: community_and_peer_interaction
per_column.rationale: Well-separated levels (vibrant_community → isolated_experience) with manageable NULLs; a meaningful associational dimension for satisfaction.

per_column.name: hands_on_learning_loss
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories, though dominated by 'not_applicable_to_subject' (130) plus many NULLs, so usable groups are thinner; still supports comparison within applicable subjects.

per_column.name: digital_tools_enabling_new_learning
per_column.rationale: Three clear, well-balanced categories capturing a distinct theme; good for segmenting and comparing against satisfaction.

per_column.name: asynchronous_pacing_autonomy
per_column.rationale: Interpretable ordered categories around pacing autonomy; some sparse tails (self_paced_empowering=8) but overall a valid segmentation variable.

per_column.name: teacher_responsiveness_and_support
per_column.rationale: Meaningful responsiveness gradient, though nearly half are NULL (103), weakening coverage; remaining categories are interpretable and comparable.

per_column.name: material_resources_and_supplies
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories but heavily dominated by 'not_applicable' (173), leaving small cells; limited but non-trivial comparative value.

judge.rationale: As a set, the added columns extract distinct, human-interpretable open-response themes (adaptation, instructional depth, participation barriers, community, digital tools, pacing, responsiveness, resources), each with named, well-separated categories rather than opaque scores. None merely restate the satisfaction focus, and they are genuine associational variables one can group on and cross-tabulate against satisfaction by role/grade/subject, directly serving the exploratory query. Informativeness is reduced (not maximal) because several columns are dominated by a single 'not_applicable'/'not_present'/NULL bucket (hands_on_learning_loss, material_resources, teacher_responsiveness), which thins the comparable groups and limits meaningful segmentation for those fields.
